lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about childhood, when we were children.
When I was little, I lived with my grandmother. I loved it.
Go on. What was her house like?
A big garden, a small kitchen, and a cat. I played in the garden every day.
I remember my first bike. It was red. I rode it to school every day. I fell over ten times, and got up ten times.
Ten times? Poor Sam.
I looked at the road, and I fell over. Then I looked at the sky, and I fell over.
[laugh] And your toys?
I had one toy, a small brown dog. And one game: football. I loved both.
Where is the dog now?
In my bedroom. He is still there. He is grown up, too.
A grown-up toy dog. Bye for now!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is childhood memories.
Let's begin. What's your best memory?
The playground near my school. We used to go out there every afternoon. On weekends, we got up early and played football until it was dark.
Did your parents call you home?
My mum did. From the window. She had a very loud voice. The whole street knew my name. She never punished me, she just shouted.
[laugh] My grandparents brought me up. They had a few rules. No sweets before dinner. No TV after nine.
Did you follow the rules?
No. I stayed up with a torch under the blanket. I read all night. Those were the days.
Imagine, now we stay up for work, and we have no torch.
It was a long time ago, but I remember everything. Even the secret place behind the house.
I had a secret place, too. It was a box under the bed. It had a lot of sweets.
Your mum knew.
She always knew. See you next time!

words.phrase: It was a long time ago.

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is childhood, and the stories everybody tells at family dinners.
Mine: when I was seven, I shared a room with my sister. We had an imaginary country. It had its own flag and its own law.
What was the law?
Number one: no brothers. We had a brother. So he was in prison, in the wardrobe.
[laugh] And you got away with it?
For one day. Then my mum opened the wardrobe. Back in the day, she was very strict.
My upbringing was carefree. My parents spoiled me a little. But you were mischievous, I think.
Very. Strict parents make clever children.
My parents were more relaxed. My dad taught me to dance when I was four. I look back on it as the happiest and most embarrassing time of my life.
Do you have a scar from childhood?
Yes, on my knee. I fell off my bike. It was the day I got my first bike. It happened like it was yesterday.
Some people grow up. I never really did. I still hide in the wardrobe when there's a family argument.
Nostalgia is a funny thing. You don't remember the rain. You remember the toys and the cake.
A trip down memory lane is sweet. But the rain is never in the photos.
A question for our listeners: what was your favourite place as a child?
Mine: my grandmother's sofa. See you next time!
